question: According to the manual, what distinguishes a 'vehicle emergency' from a 'traffic emergency'?
choice_a: A vehicle emergency only refers to running out of fuel
choice_b: A vehicle emergency happens when two vehicles are about to collide
choice_c: A vehicle emergency occurs when tires, brakes, or other critical parts fail
choice_d: There is no difference between the two terms
explanation: The manual states traffic emergencies occur when two vehicles are about to collide, while vehicle emergencies occur when tires, brakes, or other critical parts fail.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Driving Emergencies

question: Why does the manual say that steering away from an obstacle can be safer than stopping in an emergency?
choice_a: Steering never risks losing control of the vehicle
choice_b: Steering activates the ABS system automatically
choice_c: Brakes are unreliable on all commercial vehicles
choice_d: You can almost always turn to miss an obstacle more quickly than you can stop
explanation: The manual explains that stopping is not always the safest action, since you can almost always turn to miss an obstacle more quickly than you can stop, though top-heavy vehicles and tractors with multiple trailers may flip over.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Driving Emergencies

question: What is 'counter-steering,' as described in the manual?
choice_a: Steering only with the parking brake engaged
choice_b: A technique used only when ABS has failed
choice_c: Turning the steering wheel back in the other direction once you've passed whatever was in your path
choice_d: Braking and steering at the exact same instant
explanation: The manual describes counter-steering as turning the wheel back the other way after passing an obstacle, and says emergency steering and counter-steering should be thought of as two parts of one driving action.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Driving Emergencies

question: If an oncoming driver has drifted into your lane, which direction does the manual recommend steering?
choice_a: It never matters which way you steer
choice_b: Left, into the oncoming driver's original lane
choice_c: Right
choice_d: Directly at the oncoming vehicle to force it to react
explanation: The manual states that if an oncoming driver has drifted into your lane, a move to your right is best, since the driver's natural response will likely be to return to their own lane.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Driving Emergencies

question: If you are blocked on both sides by other vehicles and must steer to avoid a crash, what does the manual recommend?
choice_a: Steer left, even if it means entering an opposing traffic lane
choice_b: Stop instantly regardless of following distance
choice_c: Steer toward whichever vehicle appears smaller
choice_d: A move to the right may be best, since it avoids forcing anyone into an opposing traffic lane
explanation: The manual states that if you are blocked on both sides, a move to the right may be best, because at least you won't force anyone into an opposing traffic lane and a possible head-on collision.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Driving Emergencies

question: If you must leave the road in an emergency, what does the manual say about braking?
choice_a: Avoid braking, if possible, until your speed has dropped to about 20 mph, then brake very gently
choice_b: Never touch the brakes until you have come to a complete stop on your own
choice_c: Brake as hard as possible the instant you leave the pavement
choice_d: Use only the parking brake the entire time
explanation: The manual advises avoiding the brakes until speed has dropped to about 20 mph, then braking very gently to avoid skidding on a loose surface.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Driving Emergencies

question: When returning to the road after driving onto the shoulder, why does the manual warn against edging back onto the pavement gradually?
choice_a: Your tires might grab unexpectedly and you could lose control
choice_b: It takes too much time
choice_c: It will trigger the ABS malfunction lamp
choice_d: It is illegal to return to the road gradually
explanation: The manual warns that edging gradually back onto the road can cause the tires to grab unexpectedly, resulting in loss of control; instead, you should turn sharply enough to get back on safely, then counter-steer immediately.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Driving Emergencies

question: With the 'controlled braking' method for stopping quickly, how should you apply the brakes?
choice_a: Gradually increasing pressure over ten seconds
choice_b: As hard as you can without locking the wheels, keeping steering movements small
choice_c: Only using the parking brake
choice_d: In short, rapid taps regardless of wheel lockup
explanation: Controlled braking means applying the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels while keeping steering movements small; if a bigger adjustment is needed or the wheels lock, you release and then reapply the brakes.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Driving Emergencies

question: With the 'stab braking' method, when should you fully reapply the brakes after releasing them?
choice_a: Never reapply them once released
choice_b: Immediately, without any delay
choice_c: Only after the vehicle has completely stopped
choice_d: As soon as the wheels start rolling again
explanation: Stab braking involves applying the brakes fully, releasing when the wheels lock, and reapplying fully as soon as the wheels start rolling again; it can take up to one second for the wheels to start rolling after release.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Driving Emergencies

question: Why does jamming the brake pedal down as hard as possible fail as an emergency braking technique?
choice_a: It has no real drawback and is recommended
choice_b: It keeps the wheels locked up, causing a skid and loss of control
choice_c: It automatically shifts the transmission into neutral
choice_d: It wastes brake fluid unnecessarily
explanation: The manual states that emergency braking does not mean pushing the pedal as hard as you can, since that only keeps the wheels locked and causes a skid, and skidding wheels cannot be controlled.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Driving Emergencies

question: According to the manual, most hydraulic brake failures occur for which two reasons?
choice_a: Dead battery and faulty starter
choice_b: Worn tires and poor wheel alignment
choice_c: Overinflated tires and a clogged air filter
choice_d: Loss of hydraulic pressure and brake fade on long hills
explanation: The manual lists loss of hydraulic pressure and brake fade on long hills as the two main reasons for most hydraulic brake failures.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Driving Emergencies

question: If your brake pedal feels spongy or goes to the floor from loss of hydraulic pressure, what actions does the manual suggest?
choice_a: Turn off the engine and let the vehicle roll to a stop
choice_b: Accelerate to try to build hydraulic pressure back up
choice_c: Shift into neutral and coast to a stop
choice_d: Pump the brake pedal and use the parking/emergency brake, adjusting pressure with the release button or lever
explanation: The manual suggests pumping the brakes to generate hydraulic pressure and using the parking/emergency brake, which is a separate system, while pressing the release button or pulling the release lever to adjust brake pressure and prevent wheel lockup.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Driving Emergencies

question: If your brakes fail on a long downgrade, what does the manual say is your best hope for stopping safely?
choice_a: Honking the horn continuously
choice_b: An escape ramp
choice_c: Shifting the transmission into reverse
choice_d: Turning off the engine
explanation: The manual states that once brakes have failed on a downgrade, your best hope is an escape ramp, and if one is available with signs directing you to it, you should use it.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Driving Emergencies

question: Which of the following is listed in the manual as a warning sign of tire failure?
choice_a: The engine temperature gauge reading lower than normal
choice_b: A loud 'bang,' heavy vibration or thumping, or unusually heavy steering feel
choice_c: A sudden increase in fuel economy
choice_d: The ABS malfunction lamp turning off
explanation: The manual lists sound (a loud bang), vibration or thumping, and a heavy steering feel as the major signs of tire failure.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Driving Emergencies

question: If a tire fails while you are driving, what does the manual say you should do about the brakes?
choice_a: Stay off the brake until the vehicle has slowed down, then brake gently
choice_b: Use only the parking brake for the rest of the trip
choice_c: Pump the brakes continuously from the moment of failure
choice_d: Brake as hard as possible immediately
explanation: The manual warns that braking when a tire has failed could cause loss of control, so unless you are about to hit something, you should stay off the brake until the vehicle has slowed down, then brake gently.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Driving Emergencies

question: After a suspected tire failure and once you've come to a stop, what does the manual say you should always do?
choice_a: Get out and check all the tires, even if the vehicle seems to be handling all right
choice_b: Wait for roadside assistance before touching anything
choice_c: Continue driving until the next scheduled inspection
choice_d: Only inspect the tire on the side you felt the vibration
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to get out and check all the tires after stopping, even if the vehicle seems fine, since with dual tires the only way you may know one has failed is by looking at it.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Driving Emergencies

question: What does the Antilock Braking System (ABS) do, according to the manual?
choice_a: It increases your normal braking capability
choice_b: It applies the parking brake without driver input
choice_c: It automatically steers the vehicle around obstacles
choice_d: It keeps your wheels from locking up during hard brake applications
explanation: The manual defines ABS as a computerized system that keeps the wheels from locking up during hard brake applications; it is an addition to normal brakes, not a replacement.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: Does ABS necessarily shorten your stopping distance, according to the manual?
choice_a: Yes, it always cuts stopping distance roughly in half
choice_b: Yes, but only on dry pavement
choice_c: No, but it helps you keep the vehicle under control during hard braking
choice_d: No, ABS has no effect on braking at all
explanation: The manual explicitly states that ABS does not necessarily shorten stopping distance, but it does help you keep the vehicle under control during hard braking.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: How does an ABS system detect and respond to potential wheel lockup?
choice_a: A mechanical valve in the transmission shifts to a lower gear
choice_b: The driver manually adjusts a dashboard brake-pressure dial
choice_c: The parking brake automatically engages
choice_d: Sensors detect potential wheel lockup and an electronic control unit (ECU) decreases brake pressure to avoid it
explanation: The manual explains that sensors detect potential wheel lockup, and the ECU decreases brake pressure to avoid it, adjusting pressure to provide maximum braking without danger of lockup.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: Per the manual, truck tractors with air brakes are required to have ABS if built on or after:
choice_a: March 1, 1999
choice_b: March 1, 1998
choice_c: January 1, 1990
choice_d: March 1, 1997
explanation: The Department of Transportation requires ABS on truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: Per the manual, hydraulically braked trucks and buses with a GVWR of 10,000 lbs or more are required to have ABS if built on or after:
choice_a: March 1, 1998
choice_b: March 1, 1999
choice_c: March 1, 1997
choice_d: March 1, 2000
explanation: The manual states hydraulically braked trucks and buses with a GVWR of 10,000 lbs or more built on or after March 1, 1999, are required to have ABS.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: How can you tell if a tractor, truck, or bus is equipped with ABS?
choice_a: It will have a green indicator light on the dashboard
choice_b: It will have an extra brake pedal on the passenger side
choice_c: There is no way to tell without disassembling the brakes
choice_d: It will have a yellow ABS malfunction lamp on the instrument panel
explanation: Tractors, trucks, and buses with ABS will have yellow ABS malfunction lamps on the instrument panel.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: On a trailer equipped with ABS, where is the yellow malfunction lamp typically located?
choice_a: Inside the cargo compartment
choice_b: On the rear bumper, centered
choice_c: On the left side, either on the front or rear corner
choice_d: On the dashboard of the towing vehicle only
explanation: The manual states trailers will have yellow ABS malfunction lamps on the left side, either on the front or rear corner.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: If the ABS malfunction lamp stays on after the startup bulb check, or comes on while you are driving, what does this indicate?
choice_a: The parking brake is engaged
choice_b: The vehicle is functioning perfectly
choice_c: You may have lost ABS control
choice_d: The tires need to be rotated immediately
explanation: The manual states that if the malfunction lamp stays on after the bulb check, or comes on once you're under way, you may have lost ABS control.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: According to the manual, when the steering wheels lock up on a vehicle without ABS during hard braking on a slippery surface, what happens?
choice_a: You lose steering control
choice_b: Nothing changes compared to normal braking
choice_c: The vehicle automatically stops faster
choice_d: The parking brake engages automatically
explanation: The manual explains that when your steering wheels lock up, you lose steering control, and when other wheels lock up, you may skid, jackknife, or spin the vehicle.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: If only the tractor of a combination vehicle has ABS and the trailer begins to swing out during braking, what does the manual advise?
choice_a: Let up on the brakes, if you can safely do so
choice_b: Brake harder immediately to regain control
choice_c: Steer sharply into the direction the trailer is swinging
choice_d: Accelerate to pull the trailer straight
explanation: When only the tractor has ABS, the manual advises watching the trailer and letting up on the brakes, if it can be done safely, if the trailer begins to swing out.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: When braking a vehicle equipped with ABS under normal driving conditions, the manual advises you to:
choice_a: Brake as you always have, using only the braking force necessary to stop safely and stay in control
choice_b: Pump the brakes rapidly at all times
choice_c: Rely solely on the parking brake
choice_d: Always apply full brake pressure, regardless of conditions
explanation: The manual states that with ABS you should brake as you always have, using only the braking force necessary to stop safely and stay in control, regardless of whether ABS is on the tractor, trailer, or both.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: What is the one exception the manual gives where a driver may fully apply the brakes in an emergency stop?
choice_a: Whenever the parking brake has failed
choice_b: Whenever the road is wet
choice_c: When driving a straight truck or combination with working ABS on all axles
choice_d: When towing an unbraked trailer
explanation: The manual states that if you drive a straight truck or combination with working ABS on all axles, you can fully apply the brakes in an emergency stop.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: Which of the following correctly reflects one of the manual's ABS safety reminders?
choice_a: ABS won't prevent power or turning skids caused by spinning the drive wheels or going too fast in a turn
choice_b: ABS will always shorten your stopping distance
choice_c: ABS eliminates the need for a safe, careful driver
choice_d: ABS will allow you to follow other vehicles more closely
explanation: The manual's safety reminders state ABS won't prevent power or turning skids -- it should prevent brake-induced skids or jackknifes, but not those caused by spinning the drive wheels or going too fast in a turn.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: According to the manual's ABS safety reminders, what remains 'the best vehicle safety feature'?
choice_a: Dual rear tires
choice_b: A safe driver
choice_c: A properly charged fire extinguisher
choice_d: An escape ramp
explanation: The manual's ABS safety reminders conclude by stating that the best vehicle safety feature is still a safe driver.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: According to the manual, a skid happens whenever:
choice_a: The vehicle exceeds the posted speed limit
choice_b: The tires lose their grip on the road
choice_c: The ABS malfunction lamp illuminates
choice_d: The parking brake is applied while moving slowly
explanation: The manual defines a skid as happening whenever the tires lose their grip on the road.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Skid Control and Recovery

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four causes of skids listed in the manual?
choice_a: Over-braking
choice_b: Under-inflated tires
choice_c: Driving too fast for conditions
choice_d: Over-steering
explanation: The manual lists over-braking, over-steering, over-acceleration, and driving too fast as the four causes of skids; under-inflated tires is not listed among them.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Skid Control and Recovery

question: According to the manual, most serious skids result from:
choice_a: Worn windshield wipers
choice_b: Driving too fast for road conditions
choice_c: Using cruise control on the highway
choice_d: Poor radio reception
explanation: The manual states that most serious skids result from driving too fast for road conditions.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Skid Control and Recovery

question: What causes an 'over-acceleration' skid, as defined in the manual?
choice_a: Driving downhill too slowly
choice_b: Using the parking brake while accelerating
choice_c: Supplying too much power to the drive wheels, causing them to spin
choice_d: Riding the clutch at a stop
explanation: The manual defines over-acceleration as supplying too much power to the drive wheels, causing them to spin.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Skid Control and Recovery

question: What is the most common type of skid, according to the manual?
choice_a: A front-wheel skid caused by worn wiper blades
choice_b: A skid caused only by strong crosswinds
choice_c: A drive-wheel skid, where the rear wheels lose traction through excessive braking or acceleration
choice_d: A skid caused by an empty fuel tank
explanation: The manual states that by far the most common skid is one in which the rear wheels lose traction through excessive braking or acceleration.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Skid Control and Recovery

question: If a drive-wheel skid caused by acceleration occurs on ice or snow, what usually stops it, according to the manual?
choice_a: Flooring the accelerator to power through it
choice_b: Taking your foot off the accelerator
choice_c: Turning on your headlights
choice_d: Applying the parking brake hard
explanation: The manual states that skids caused by acceleration usually happen on ice or snow, and taking your foot off the accelerator can easily stop them.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Skid Control and Recovery

question: With vehicles towing trailers, a drive-wheel skid can cause the trailer to push the towing vehicle sideways, resulting in:
choice_a: A sudden jackknife
choice_b: A tire blowout
choice_c: An ABS malfunction
choice_d: Brake fade
explanation: The manual explains that with vehicles towing trailers, a drive-wheel skid can let the trailer push the towing vehicle sideways, causing a sudden jackknife.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Skid Control and Recovery

question: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, what two actions does the manual recommend?
choice_a: Stop braking to let the rear wheels roll again, then counter-steer
choice_b: Shift immediately into the highest available gear
choice_c: Accelerate hard out of the skid
choice_d: Brake harder while holding the wheel perfectly straight
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to stop braking, which lets the rear wheels roll again, and to counter-steer, since the vehicle will otherwise keep turning as it comes back on course.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Skid Control and Recovery

question: According to the manual, what primarily causes most front-wheel skids?
choice_a: Driving too fast for conditions
choice_b: Low fuel levels
choice_c: A dirty windshield
choice_d: Overinflated front tires
explanation: The manual states that driving too fast for conditions causes most front-wheel skids, with lack of front tire tread and improper cargo weight distribution as other causes.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Skid Control and Recovery

question: In a front-wheel skid, how does the vehicle typically behave, according to the manual?
choice_a: It automatically corrects itself within seconds
choice_b: It spins in a complete circle
choice_c: It stops immediately
choice_d: The front end tends to go in a straight line regardless of how much you turn the steering wheel
explanation: The manual describes a front-wheel skid as one in which the front end tends to go in a straight line no matter how much you turn the wheel.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Skid Control and Recovery

question: How does the manual say you should stop a front-wheel skid?
choice_a: Stop turning and/or braking so hard, and slow down as quickly as possible without skidding
choice_b: Shift into neutral and coast
choice_c: Turn the steering wheel more sharply
choice_d: Accelerate until traction returns
explanation: The manual states that the only way to stop a front-wheel skid is to let the vehicle slow down by stopping turning and/or braking so hard.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Skid Control and Recovery

question: According to the manual, what are the three basic steps to take at any accident where you are not seriously hurt?
choice_a: Turn off your radio, check your mirrors, and drive away
choice_b: Move all vehicles immediately, determine fault, wait for police
choice_c: Call your dispatcher, photograph the scene, exchange insurance information
choice_d: Protect the area, notify authorities, care for the injured
explanation: The manual states the basic steps at any accident are to protect the area, notify authorities, and care for the injured.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Accident Procedures

question: If your vehicle is involved in an accident, what should you try to do first to protect the area?
choice_a: Leave it exactly where it stopped, no matter the location
choice_b: Begin repairs on the vehicle immediately
choice_c: Unload all cargo before doing anything else
choice_d: Get it to the side of the road to help prevent another accident and allow traffic to move
explanation: The manual advises getting your vehicle to the side of the road if it is involved in the accident, to help prevent another accident and allow traffic to move.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Accident Procedures

question: If you are stopping to help at someone else's accident, where does the manual say you should park?
choice_a: Directly behind the wrecked vehicles
choice_b: In the opposing lane, facing traffic
choice_c: Away from the accident, since the area immediately around it will be needed for emergency vehicles
choice_d: As close as possible to help block other traffic
explanation: The manual advises parking away from the accident if you're stopping to help, since the area immediately around the accident will be needed for emergency vehicles.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Accident Procedures

question: What does the manual say you should do to warn other traffic after an accident?
choice_a: Nothing additional is needed, since other drivers will see the wreckage
choice_b: Stand in the roadway and wave your arms
choice_c: Sound your horn continuously until help arrives
choice_d: Turn on your flashers and set out reflective triangles so other drivers can see them in time to avoid the accident
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to put on their flashers and set out reflective triangles, making sure other drivers can see them in time to avoid the accident.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Accident Procedures

question: If you have a cell phone or CB radio after an accident, what does the manual advise?
choice_a: Avoid using it in case it becomes evidence
choice_b: Only call your employer, never the police
choice_c: Wait until you've fully inspected all vehicles before calling anyone
choice_d: Call for assistance before you get out of your vehicle
explanation: The manual advises that if you have a cell phone or CB, you should call for assistance before you get out of your vehicle.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Accident Procedures

question: If you do not have a phone after an accident, what does the manual say you should do?
choice_a: Assume that another passing driver will call for help
choice_b: Wait until the accident scene has been properly protected, then phone or send someone to phone the police
choice_c: Drive directly to the nearest hospital
choice_d: Leave the scene immediately to find a phone
explanation: The manual states that without a phone, you should wait until the accident scene has been properly protected, then phone or send someone to phone the police, determining your exact location first.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Accident Procedures

question: When caring for a severely injured person at an accident scene, when does the manual say you should avoid moving them?
choice_a: Moving them is always recommended for their comfort
choice_b: Unless the danger of fire or passing traffic makes it necessary
choice_c: Only if they specifically ask to be moved
choice_d: You should never move them under any circumstance
explanation: The manual advises not moving a severely injured person unless the danger of fire or passing traffic makes it necessary.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Accident Procedures

question: How does the manual say you should try to stop heavy bleeding in an injured person at an accident scene?
choice_a: Apply direct pressure to the wound
choice_b: Give them water to drink
choice_c: Elevate only their feet
choice_d: Wrap them tightly and wait without further action
explanation: The manual instructs stopping heavy bleeding by applying direct pressure to the wound.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Accident Procedures

question: Besides addressing bleeding, what other basic care does the manual say to give an injured person while awaiting help?
choice_a: Keep the injured person warm
choice_b: Encourage them to walk around to stay alert
choice_c: Offer them food
choice_d: Remove their protective clothing
explanation: The manual's simple steps for assisting the injured include keeping the injured person warm.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Accident Procedures

question: Which of the following is listed in the manual as a cause of tire-related vehicle fires?
choice_a: Overinflated tires and mismatched tread brands
choice_b: Tires rotated too frequently
choice_c: Under-inflated tires and duals that touch
choice_d: New tires that haven't been broken in
explanation: The manual lists under-inflated tires and duals that touch as causes of tire-related fires.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Fires

question: As part of fire-prevention vehicle inspections, the manual says you should be sure to check that:
choice_a: The radio and infotainment system work properly
choice_b: The fire extinguisher is charged
choice_c: The spare tire matches the others in tread pattern
choice_d: The cargo is fully insured
explanation: The manual's fire prevention section instructs drivers to make a complete inspection of the electrical, fuel, exhaust systems, tires, and cargo, and to be sure the fire extinguisher is charged.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Fires

question: If your vehicle catches fire, what is the first step the manual recommends?
choice_a: Open all doors and windows immediately, then keep driving
choice_b: Pull off the road and park in an open area, away from buildings, trees, brush, or other vehicles
choice_c: Drive directly to the nearest service station
choice_d: Continue driving to the nearest exit ramp regardless of surroundings
explanation: The manual's first fire-fighting step is to pull off the road and park in an open area away from buildings, trees, brush, other vehicles, or anything else that might catch fire.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Fires

question: According to the manual, when finding a place to stop a burning vehicle, what should you specifically avoid?
choice_a: Pulling into a service station
choice_b: Turning off the engine
choice_c: Parking in an open area
choice_d: Notifying emergency services of your location
explanation: The manual explicitly instructs, 'Don't pull into a service station!' when stopping a vehicle that is on fire.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Fires

question: With an engine fire, what does the manual say about the hood and how to fight the fire?
choice_a: Prop the hood open to help ventilate the fire
choice_b: Open the hood immediately to assess the damage
choice_c: Remove the hood entirely before doing anything else
choice_d: Don't open the hood if you can avoid it, and shoot foam through louvers, the radiator, or from underneath
explanation: The manual advises turning off the engine as soon as possible, avoiding opening the hood if possible, and shooting foam through louvers, the radiator, or the vehicle's underside.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Fires

question: For a cargo fire in a van or box trailer, especially one carrying hazardous materials, what does the manual say about the doors?
choice_a: Remove the doors from their hinges
choice_b: Open them fully right away to let smoke escape
choice_c: It makes no difference whether the doors are open or shut
choice_d: Keep them shut, since opening them supplies oxygen and can make the fire burn very fast
explanation: The manual warns to keep the doors shut on a van or box trailer cargo fire, especially with hazardous materials, since opening the doors supplies oxygen and can cause the fire to burn very fast.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Fires

question: When using a fire extinguisher, where does the manual say you should aim it?
choice_a: It doesn't matter where you aim, as long as you're close
choice_b: At the smoke rising above the fire
choice_c: At the source or base of the fire
choice_d: Up into the flames themselves
explanation: The manual instructs aiming the extinguisher at the source or base of the fire, not up into the flames.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Fires

question: Why does the manual say you should not use water on a gasoline fire?
choice_a: It causes an electrical shock
choice_b: It has no effect on the fire either way
choice_c: Water itself is flammable
choice_d: It will spread the flames
explanation: The manual states that water should not be used on a gasoline fire because it will spread the flames.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Fires

question: Why does the manual say you should not use water on an electrical fire?
choice_a: It puts the fire out too quickly to be safe
choice_b: It will spread the flames
choice_c: It can cause a shock
choice_d: It permanently damages the wiring
explanation: The manual warns that water should not be used on an electrical fire because it can cause shock.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Fires

question: According to the manual, what does putting out a burning tire require?
choice_a: Non-conducting agents only
choice_b: Cooling, and lots of water may be required
choice_c: Specialized combustible-metal powder
choice_d: Smothering with dry chemical only
explanation: The manual states that a burning tire must be cooled, and lots of water may be required.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Fires

question: If you're not sure what extinguishing agent to use on a fire, especially a hazardous materials fire, what does the manual advise?
choice_a: Try water first, and switch agents if that doesn't work
choice_b: Use whatever extinguisher is closest at hand
choice_c: Attempt to smother the fire with fuel-soaked rags
choice_d: Wait for firefighters
explanation: The manual advises that if you're not sure what to use, especially on a hazardous materials fire, you should wait for firefighters.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Fires

question: Per the fire class table (Figure 2.20), a Class A fire (wood, paper, ordinary combustibles) should be extinguished by:
choice_a: Never using water under any circumstances
choice_b: Cooling and quenching using water or dry chemicals
choice_c: Non-conducting agents only
choice_d: Specialized combustible-metal powders
explanation: Figure 2.20 in the manual states Class A fires (wood, paper, ordinary combustibles) should be extinguished by cooling and quenching using water or dry chemicals.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Fires

question: Per the fire class table (Figure 2.20), a Class C fire (electrical equipment) should be extinguished with:
choice_a: Water only
choice_b: Foam exclusively
choice_c: Sand or dirt only
choice_d: Non-conducting agents such as carbon dioxide or dry chemicals -- do not use water
explanation: Figure 2.20 states Class C (electrical equipment) fires should be extinguished with non-conducting agents such as carbon dioxide or dry chemicals, and specifically says do not use water.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Fires

question: Per the fire class table (Figure 2.20), Class D fires (fires in combustible metals) should be extinguished using:
choice_a: Carbon dioxide only
choice_b: Specialized extinguishing powders
choice_c: Foam
choice_d: Ordinary water
explanation: Figure 2.20 states that Class D fires, in combustible metals, should be extinguished by using specialized extinguishing powders.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Fires

question: According to Figure 2.21 in the manual, which extinguisher type is listed as effective on all four classes of fire (A, B, C, and D)?
choice_a: Purple K Dry Chemical
choice_b: Regular Dry Chemical
choice_c: Multi-Purpose Dry Chemical
choice_d: Halogenated Agent (Gas)
explanation: Figure 2.21 lists Multi-Purpose Dry Chemical as the extinguisher type usable on Class A, B, C, and D fires.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Fires

question: According to the manual, which of the following does alcohol impair?
choice_a: Muscle coordination, reaction time, depth perception, and night vision
choice_b: Only your sense of smell
choice_c: Only your sense of hearing
choice_d: Nothing, if a person has built up a tolerance
explanation: The manual states alcohol impairs muscle coordination, reaction time, depth perception, and night vision, and affects the parts of the brain that control judgment and inhibition.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Alcohol, Other Drugs, and Driving

question: How does alcohol travel through the body after it is consumed, according to the manual?
choice_a: It bypasses the bloodstream entirely
choice_b: It goes directly into the bloodstream and is carried to the brain
choice_c: It only ever affects the stomach lining
choice_d: It is fully digested like food before reaching the brain
explanation: The manual explains that alcohol goes directly into the blood stream and is carried to the brain.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Alcohol, Other Drugs, and Driving

question: According to the manual, roughly how much alcohol can the liver process per hour?
choice_a: About one-third of an ounce
choice_b: One full standard drink
choice_c: Two standard drinks
choice_d: There is no processing limit
explanation: The manual states the liver can only process about one-third of an ounce of alcohol per hour, which is considerably less than the alcohol in a standard drink.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Alcohol, Other Drugs, and Driving

question: According to the manual, what is the only thing that will actually sober a person up?
choice_a: Black coffee
choice_b: A cold shower
choice_c: Time
choice_d: Vigorous exercise
explanation: The manual states that because the liver processes alcohol at a fixed rate, only time -- not black coffee or a cold shower -- will sober you up.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Alcohol, Other Drugs, and Driving

question: Which set of drinks does the manual say contain roughly the same amount of alcohol?
choice_a: A 12-ounce glass of 5% beer, a 5-ounce glass of 12% wine, and a 1.5-ounce shot of 80-proof liquor
choice_b: Any drink, regardless of size or alcohol proof
choice_c: A 12-ounce glass of wine and a 5-ounce glass of beer
choice_d: Only beer and liquor, but never wine
explanation: The manual lists a 12-oz glass of 5% beer, a 5-oz glass of 12% wine, and a 1.5-oz shot of 80-proof liquor as containing the same amount of alcohol.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Alcohol, Other Drugs, and Driving

question: According to the manual, what three factors determine Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC)?
choice_a: Time of day, type of vehicle, and food eaten that day
choice_b: Amount of alcohol consumed, how fast you drink it, and your body weight
choice_c: Age, gender, and years of driving experience
choice_d: Only the total number of drinks consumed
explanation: The manual states BAC is determined by the amount of alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Alcohol, Other Drugs, and Driving

question: According to the manual, which part of the brain is affected first as BAC builds up?
choice_a: The part controlling long-term memory
choice_b: The part controlling vision only
choice_c: The part controlling heart rate
choice_d: The part controlling judgment and self-control
explanation: The manual states that the first part of the brain affected as BAC builds up controls judgment and self-control.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Alcohol, Other Drugs, and Driving

question: Why is it especially dangerous, according to the manual, that alcohol affects judgment and self-control first?
choice_a: It only affects passengers, never the driver
choice_b: It has no real bearing on driving safety
choice_c: It can keep drinkers from realizing they are getting drunk
choice_d: It causes immediate unconsciousness
explanation: The manual notes that one of the bad things about judgment being affected first is that it can keep drinkers from knowing they are getting drunk.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Alcohol, Other Drugs, and Driving

question: Per the manual's BAC effects table, a BAC of .08 is described as:
choice_a: The point at which most people lose consciousness
choice_b: A level with no noticeable effects
choice_c: A mellow feeling with slight body warmth
choice_d: The drunk driving limit, with definite impairment in coordination and judgment
explanation: The manual's BAC effects table lists .08 as the drunk driving limit, with definite impairment in coordination and judgment.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Alcohol, Other Drugs, and Driving

question: Per the manual's BAC effects table, at which BAC level is a person described as having impaired balance and movement, 'clearly drunk,' and 'unable to drive'?
explanation: The manual's BAC effects table lists .15 as the level with impaired balance and movement, clearly drunk, and unable to drive.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Alcohol, Other Drugs, and Driving

question: Which of the following is listed in the manual as an effect of alcohol on driving behavior?
choice_a: Increased attentiveness to road hazards
choice_b: Improved night vision
choice_c: Faster reaction time to hazards
choice_d: Straddling lanes and running stop signs or red lights
explanation: The manual lists straddling lanes, quick jerky starts, not signaling, and running stop signs and red lights among the effects of alcohol on driving.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Alcohol, Other Drugs, and Driving

question: Which substances does the manual specifically name as prohibited while a driver is on duty, besides alcohol?
choice_a: Only illegal street drugs
choice_b: Controlled substances, amphetamines ('pep pills,' 'uppers'), narcotics, or any substance that could make the driver unsafe
choice_c: Only prescription medications with no exceptions
choice_d: Only over-the-counter cold medicine
explanation: The manual states laws prohibit being under the influence of any controlled substance, amphetamines such as pep pills or uppers, narcotics, or any other substance that can make the driver unsafe.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Alcohol, Other Drugs, and Driving

question: According to the manual, when is possession and use of a doctor-prescribed drug permitted for a driver?
choice_a: Only on weekends when not scheduled to drive
choice_b: Never, all prescription drugs are banned while driving
choice_c: If the doctor informs the driver that it will not affect safe driving ability
choice_d: Only with written employer approval
explanation: The manual states possession and use of a drug given to a driver by a doctor is permitted if the doctor informs the driver that it will not affect safe driving ability.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Alcohol, Other Drugs, and Driving

question: Why does the manual warn against using drugs that 'hide fatigue'?
choice_a: They interact badly with food
choice_b: They are always illegal to possess
choice_c: They are more expensive than caffeine
choice_d: The only real cure for fatigue is rest
explanation: The manual warns not to use any drug that hides fatigue, since the only cure for fatigue is rest.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Alcohol, Other Drugs, and Driving

question: If you become too ill to operate your vehicle safely, what does the manual say you must do?
choice_a: Pull over and wait exactly one hour before continuing
choice_b: Continue driving carefully at a reduced speed
choice_c: Not drive, except in an emergency you may drive to the nearest place you can safely stop
choice_d: Call a family member to come finish the trip for you
explanation: The manual states that if you become too ill to operate a motor vehicle safely, you must not drive, though in an emergency you may drive to the nearest place where you can safely stop.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Alcohol, Other Drugs, and Driving

question: According to the manual, what must all drivers be able to do regarding hazardous cargo, even without a hazmat endorsement?
choice_a: Personally repackage any hazardous materials found improperly packaged
choice_b: Recognize hazardous cargo and know whether they can haul it without a hazardous materials endorsement
choice_c: Refuse to ever transport any regulated product
choice_d: Memorize the entire US DOT Emergency Response Guidebook
explanation: The manual states all drivers must be able to recognize hazardous cargo and know whether or not they can haul it without a hazardous materials endorsement.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers

question: What are the three general purposes of hazardous materials rules, according to the manual?
choice_a: Train dockworkers, insure cargo, and license vehicles
choice_b: Track fuel usage, enforce weight limits, and issue placards
choice_c: Contain the product, communicate the risk, and ensure safe drivers and equipment
choice_d: Reduce shipping costs, speed up delivery, and simplify paperwork
explanation: The manual states the intent of the hazardous materials rules is to contain the product, communicate the risk, and ensure safe drivers and equipment.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers

question: How does the manual say a shipper communicates the risk of hazardous cargo to dockworkers and drivers?
choice_a: Through a verbal phone call before pickup
choice_b: Through shipping papers and diamond-shaped hazard labels
choice_c: Through a distinct horn signal
choice_d: Through a specially colored license plate
explanation: The manual states the shipper uses shipping papers and diamond-shaped hazard labels to warn dockworkers and drivers of the risk.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers

question: Where must a driver keep hazardous materials shipping papers while driving, according to the manual?
choice_a: In a pouch on the driver's door, in clear view within reach while driving, or on the driver's seat when out of the vehicle
choice_b: In the glove compartment, out of sight
choice_c: Mailed ahead separately to the destination
choice_d: Locked in the cargo area next to the hazardous materials
explanation: The manual requires drivers to keep hazmat shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's door, in clear view within reach while driving, or on the driver's seat when out of the vehicle.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers

question: What is a placard, as described in the manual?
choice_a: A sign put on the outside of a vehicle that identifies the hazard class of the cargo
choice_b: A label placed only inside the cargo area
choice_c: A sticker placed only on the shipping papers
choice_d: A permit the driver keeps in a wallet
explanation: The manual defines placards as signs put on the outside of a vehicle that identify the hazard class of the cargo.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers

question: How many identical placards must a placarded vehicle display, and where?
choice_a: One placard is sufficient if visible from the road
choice_b: At least four identical placards, on the front, rear, and both sides
choice_c: Two, on the front and rear only
choice_d: Six placards, three per side
explanation: The manual states a placarded vehicle must have at least four identical placards, placed on the front, rear, and both sides.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers

question: What is an identification number, as used on hazardous materials placards or orange panels?
choice_a: The vehicle's VIN
choice_b: The driver's CDL number
choice_c: A two-letter state abbreviation
choice_d: A four-digit code used by first responders to identify hazardous materials
explanation: The manual defines identification numbers as a four-digit code used by first responders to identify hazardous materials, preceded by the letters 'NA' or 'UN.'
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers

question: What resource does the manual say lists chemicals along with their identification numbers?
choice_a: Section 1 of the CDL manual
choice_b: The US DOT Emergency Response Guidebook (ERG)
choice_c: The vehicle owner's manual
choice_d: The shipper's invoice only
explanation: The manual states the US DOT Emergency Response Guidebook (ERG) lists the chemicals and the identification numbers assigned to them.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers

question: Can a driver without a hazardous materials endorsement drive a vehicle carrying hazardous materials, according to the manual?
choice_a: Never, under any circumstances
choice_b: Yes, if the vehicle does not require placards
choice_c: Yes, but only at night
choice_d: Yes, but only for trips under 50 miles
explanation: The manual states you can drive a vehicle that carries hazardous materials if it does not require placards; if it requires placards, you cannot drive it without the hazardous materials endorsement.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers

question: Per the hazard class table in the manual, which hazard class covers gasoline and acetone?
choice_a: Class 3 - Flammable
choice_b: Class 1 - Explosives
choice_c: Class 8 - Corrosives
choice_d: Class 6 - Poisons
explanation: The manual's hazard class table lists gasoline and acetone as examples under Class 3, Flammable.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers

question: What does 'ORM-D' stand for in the manual's hazard class table, and what is a listed example?
choice_a: Other Regulated Material-Domestic; example: hair spray or charcoal
choice_b: Official Radioactive Material-Dangerous; example: uranium
choice_c: Overweight Rated Material-Domestic; example: heavy machinery
choice_d: Organic Refined Material-Diesel; example: fuel oil
explanation: The manual's hazard class table lists ORM-D as 'Other Regulated Material-Domestic,' with hair spray or charcoal given as examples.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers

question: What tank capacity threshold does the manual say triggers the need for a tank endorsement?
choice_a: Any size tank, as long as it carries a hazardous material
choice_b: More than 55 gallons individually, regardless of aggregate capacity
choice_c: More than 500 gallons individually, with no aggregate threshold
choice_d: An individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate capacity of 1,000 gallons or more
explanation: The manual states a tank endorsement is required for a commercial vehicle with a tank (or tanks) having an individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate capacity of 1,000 gallons or more.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers

question: Does the liquid or gas transported in a tank requiring a tank endorsement have to be a hazardous material, according to the manual?
choice_a: Only if it is a liquid, not a gas
choice_b: Only if it is flammable
choice_c: No -- the tank endorsement rule is based on tank capacity, regardless of whether the contents are hazardous
choice_d: Yes, always
explanation: The manual specifies that the liquid or gas transported in a tank meeting the capacity thresholds does not have to be a hazardous material for the tank endorsement to be required.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers

question: What does the manual say happens if you are stopped while driving a placarded vehicle without the required hazardous materials endorsement?
choice_a: You will be cited and not allowed to drive your truck, costing time and money
choice_b: Nothing, as long as you hold a valid CDL
choice_c: The cargo is simply reassigned to another driver on the spot with no penalty
choice_d: You receive only a verbal warning with no other consequence
explanation: The manual warns that driving a placarded vehicle without the hazardous materials endorsement is a crime, and if stopped you will be cited and not allowed to continue driving the truck.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers
